merges.note: Same person: the Los Angeles IWW member sentenced to five years in the California criminal-syndicalism campaign, entering Folsom July 12, 1923 — printed as both James P. Gordon and P. J. Gordon. The kept record has the fuller case; the dropped record's biography is appended so nothing is lost.

updates.append: His life dates, corrected per the curator: the University of Washington archival finding aid for his papers identifies Eugene Barnett as 1892-1973, and combined with the February 21 birthday on the contemporary prisoner birthday list his probable complete date of birth is February 21, 1892 — replacing earlier recorded dates of 1888 and a 1948 death that do not fit the finding aid. Convicted of second-degree murder after the November 11, 1919 Centralia confrontation, he received a 25-to-40-year sentence at Walla Walla (prisoner 9414) and was released in the early 1930s.
updates.note: Stored dates 1888-12-01 / 1948-02-02 conflict with the UW finding aid (1892-1973); forced with old values echoed.
Walla Walla prisoner number from the birthday list; fills only if the field is empty.

updates.append: The contemporary prisoner birthday list gives his birthday as February 5 (no birth year has surfaced) and his San Quentin number as 35768. He was convicted under the California criminal-syndicalism law in January 1922, essentially for his association with and advocacy for the IWW.
updates.note: Birthday known (Feb 5) but no year — recorded in the biography since a partial date cannot carry a day without a year.

updates.append: His full name — mangled to Francis K. McClenwgan by the optical scan of the birthday list — was Francis McClennigan, also printed F. E. McClennigan; his birthday was February 27 (no birth year has surfaced) and his San Quentin number 38125. A Los Angeles IWW activist, he was involved in defending workers prosecuted during the 1923 San Pedro maritime strike before being imprisoned himself in the California criminal-syndicalism prosecutions; his exact sentence and release date still await reconstruction.
updates.note: OCR-corrected name; number and birthday from the list.

updates.append: The contemporary prisoner birthday list gives his birthday as February 13 (no birth year has surfaced). His prisoner number was 38113 — the 88113 rendered by the optical scan of the list was an error. Sentenced to five years under the California criminal-syndicalism campaign, he entered Folsom on July 12, 1923 and apparently remained until his term expired.
updates.note: Runs after the merge; number corrected from the OCR reading.

updates.append: A scholarly history identifies him as 27 years old during his spring 1922 prosecution, which — his February birthday having passed — establishes an 1895 birth year; the prisoner birthday list gives the day as February 26 while a genealogy index gives February 29, 1895, a date that cannot exist (1895 was not a leap year), so the birth date is entered at month precision pending confirmation. A Sacramento IWW carpenter, he was convicted of criminal syndicalism with fellow Wobbly J. A. Casdorf and received a five-year sentence, imprisoned from February 17, 1922 — first at San Quentin under number 37474, later at Folsom as 12640 — and released sometime in 1925; the exact date remains unresolved.
updates.note: Birth at month precision (day disputed); Folsom number to the inmate field, San Quentin 37474 in the biography; case dates fill empty fields only.

flags: Frank Sherman, Francis McClennigan, and James P. Gordon have confirmed February birthdays (5th, 27th, 13th) but no birth years — recorded in their biographies because a date field cannot hold a day without a year; if years surface, full birth dates can enter.
Earl Firey's birth day is disputed: the prisoner list says February 26, a genealogy index says February 29, 1895 — impossible, as 1895 was not a leap year. Entered at February 1895 month precision.

Eugene Barnett's previous stored dates (born 1888-12-01, died 1948-02-02) were replaced by the UW finding aid dates; if those old values had a source worth reconciling, the echo in the deploy log preserves them.
